plan.english: Of-Good-Fame, the warrior, rose up in the night. He yoked two swift horses, crossed the river and came to the cow-stall of the foe. There the herdsmen were sleeping. Then he drove the cattle out. But a dog heard him and howled, and the herdsmen woke. Of-Good-Fame spoke to them: Herdsmen, do not tremble! I do not want your blood; I want the cattle of your master. Then he drove them home.

clauses.english: Of-Good-Fame, the warrior, rose up in the night.
He yoked two swift horses, crossed the river and came to the cow-stall of the foe.
There the herdsmen were sleeping.
Then he drove the cattle out.
But a dog heard him and howled, and the herdsmen woke.
Of-Good-Fame spoke to them:
Herdsmen, do not tremble!
I do not want your blood;
I want the cattle of your master.
Then he drove them home.

plan.english: At the ford two warriors were standing. Man-Minded asked: Who are you? I am Of-True-Fame, the son of a king. These cattle I drove from your enclosure, and I shall not give them to you. Then Man-Minded said: Let us two fight at the ford! May Father Sky see us! But Of-True-Fame said: Why should we two die at the ford? I shall give you ten horses in exchange for the cattle. Then Man-Minded took the horses, and the two swore an oath.

clauses.english: At the ford two warriors were standing.
Man-Minded asked:
Who are you?
I am Of-True-Fame, the son of a king.
These cattle I drove from your enclosure, and I shall not give them to you.
Then Man-Minded said:
Let us two fight at the ford!
May Father Sky see us!
But Of-True-Fame said:
Why should we two die at the ford?
I shall give you ten horses in exchange for the cattle.
Then Man-Minded took the horses, and the two swore an oath.

plan.english: In the house of the clan chief the warriors divided the cattle. The chief took the first share, and he gave bulls to the young men. He who had guarded the stall, to him they gave a cow and a sheep. Then the young men praised the chief: Giver of good things, may your fame be imperishable! He said: Cattle are the fame of men. Whoever drives them from the foe, may he receive a share.

clauses.english: In the house of the clan chief the warriors divided the cattle.
The chief took the first share, and he gave bulls to the young men.
He who had guarded the stall, to him they gave a cow and a sheep.
Then the young men praised the chief:
Giver of good things, may your fame be imperishable!
He said:
Cattle are the fame of men.
Whoever drives them from the foe, may he receive a share.

plan.english: At dawn a young herdsman ran to the house of his master. Master, thieves came in the night, and they drove off our cattle. I fled and came to you. The master asked: Who are the thieves? Where did they lead them? The herdsman said: They were men of Ill-Minded; they led them toward the hills. Then the master seized his spear and called his brothers: Let us pursue the thieves with swift horses!

clauses.english: At dawn a young herdsman ran to the house of his master.
Master, thieves came in the night, and they drove off our cattle.
I fled and came to you.
The master asked:
Who are the thieves?
Where did they lead them?
The herdsman said:
They were men of Ill-Minded; they led them toward the hills.
Then the master seized his spear and called his brothers:
Let us pursue the thieves with swift horses!

plan.english: The men of Of-Goodly-Fame followed the tracks of the herd. Through the fields they ran. In the evening they saw dust on a hill. Then Of-Goodly-Fame said: Brothers, the thieves are few, and we are many. Let us not fear them! Then they climbed the hill, and the thieves fled. The men drove the herd home and rejoiced.

clauses.english: The men of Of-Goodly-Fame followed the tracks of the herd.
Through the fields they ran.
In the evening they saw dust on a hill.
Then Of-Goodly-Fame said:
Brothers, the thieves are few, and we are many.
Let us not fear them!
Then they climbed the hill, and the thieves fled.
The men drove the herd home and rejoiced.

plan.english: At the feast the warriors drank sweet mead. Then Of-Divine-Race stood up and spoke: Friends, hear me! I drove a hundred cows from the stalls of the foe. Three men I struck down at the ford. Who will take this fame from me? My name is famous, and my fame is great. But an old man laughed and said: Words do not drive cattle; spears drive them.

clauses.english: At the feast the warriors drank sweet mead.
Then Of-Divine-Race stood up and spoke:
Friends, hear me!
I drove a hundred cows from the stalls of the foe.
Three men I struck down at the ford.
Who will take this fame from me?
My name is famous, and my fame is great.
But an old man laughed and said:
Words do not drive cattle; spears drive them.

plan.english: Kindly came to the house of Ill-Minded and said: Your men slew my brother. Give me a hundred cattle in exchange for my brother, or we shall come with spears. Ill-Minded answered: I owe you nothing. Your brother, a thief, came into my field. He stole my cattle, and he died. Kindly said: Then the gods will see the truth. He went to his own people.

clauses.english: Kindly came to the house of Ill-Minded and said:
Your men slew my brother.
Give me a hundred cattle in exchange for my brother, or we shall come with spears.
Ill-Minded answered:
I owe you nothing.
Your brother, a thief, came into my field.
He stole my cattle, and he died.
Kindly said:
Then the gods will see the truth.
He went to his own people.

plan.english: On the hill two armies were standing. Of-Good-Horses threw his spear. The spear wounded the master of the foes. He fell to the earth, and his blood was red on the grass. Then his men fled, and they left their cattle on the hill. Of-Good-Horses cried to his friends: Do not kill them! Drive the cattle home!

clauses.english: On the hill two armies were standing.
Of-Good-Horses threw his spear.
The spear wounded the master of the foes.
He fell to the earth, and his blood was red on the grass.
Then his men fled, and they left their cattle on the hill.
Of-Good-Horses cried to his friends:
Do not kill them!
Drive the cattle home!

plan.english: Ill-Minded lay on the earth, and Of-True-Fame stood over him. Ill-Minded said: Of-True-Fame, do not slay me! I shall give you your cattle and ten horses. Of-True-Fame said: Swear an oath! Then Ill-Minded lifted his hand toward the sky: Father Sky, hear me! If I deceive him, strike me down! Then the two men swore, and the herd went home.

clauses.english: Ill-Minded lay on the earth, and Of-True-Fame stood over him.
Ill-Minded said:
Of-True-Fame, do not slay me!
I shall give you your cattle and ten horses.
Of-True-Fame said:
Swear an oath!
Then Ill-Minded lifted his hand toward the sky:
Father Sky, hear me!
If I deceive him, strike me down!
Then the two men swore, and the herd went home.

plan.english: The old father spoke to his son: My son, you will go with the warriors. Do not tremble before the spears of the foes, and do not leave your friends. Whoever leaves his friends, to him there is no fame. Then the son went with the warriors, and on the third night he came home unharmed. He led many cows. The mother rejoiced and said: My son, you are whole! Now your name will be famous among the people.

clauses.english: The old father spoke to his son:
My son, you will go with the warriors.
Do not tremble before the spears of the foes, and do not leave your friends.
Whoever leaves his friends, to him there is no fame.
Then the son went with the warriors, and on the third night he came home unharmed.
He led many cows.
The mother rejoiced and said:
My son, you are whole!
Now your name will be famous among the people.

plan.english: When Ill-Minded drove off the cattle, snow lay on the fields. The cattle left their tracks in the snow. At dawn the shepherd caught sight of the tracks and called his master: Master, the snow points out to us the path of the thief! Then they followed the tracks to the river, and there they found the cattle and the sleeping thief. They bound the thief with a rope, and they led the cattle home. Snow is the foe of thieves.

clauses.english: When Ill-Minded drove off the cattle, snow lay on the fields.
The cattle left their tracks in the snow.
At dawn the shepherd caught sight of the tracks and called his master:
Master, the snow points out to us the path of the thief!
Then they followed the tracks to the river, and there they found the cattle and the sleeping thief.
They bound the thief with a rope, and they led the cattle home.
Snow is the foe of thieves.

plan.english: A great dog guarded the cattle of an old man. In the night three thieves crossed over the wall. The dog rose up and seized the first thief. The thieves cried out, and the old man woke. He seized his spear and stepped out of the house. He said to them: Flee, thieves! The gods protect my cattle. The thieves fled into the night, and the dog lay down again beside the stall. The old man gave it meat.

clauses.english: A great dog guarded the cattle of an old man.
In the night three thieves crossed over the wall.
The dog rose up and seized the first thief.
The thieves cried out, and the old man woke.
He seized his spear and stepped out of the house.
He said to them:
Flee, thieves!
The gods protect my cattle.
The thieves fled into the night, and the dog lay down again beside the stall.
The old man gave it meat.

plan.english: The men of the clan chief seized a young thief and bound him with ropes. His father came to the chief and spoke: Chief, release my son! He is young and does not know your strength. The chief asked: What will you give me in exchange for him? I shall give you gold and three horses. Then the chief released the young man, and the father led his son home.

clauses.english: The men of the clan chief seized a young thief and bound him with ropes.
His father came to the chief and spoke:
Chief, release my son!
He is young and does not know your strength.
The chief asked:
What will you give me in exchange for him?
I shall give you gold and three horses.
Then the chief released the young man, and the father led his son home.

plan.english: The young warriors were sitting around the fire. An old man said to them: Young men, hear my words. Cattle die, brothers die, but fame does not die. The fame of a good man is imperishable. Do not steal the cattle of a guest. Whoever deceives a guest, the gods see him. Drive the cattle of the foes, and carry your shares home!

clauses.english: The young warriors were sitting around the fire.
An old man said to them:
Young men, hear my words.
Cattle die, brothers die, but fame does not die.
The fame of a good man is imperishable.
Do not steal the cattle of a guest.
Whoever deceives a guest, the gods see him.
Drive the cattle of the foes, and carry your shares home!

plan.english: Of-Good-Fame came with his men to a great river. Its water was deep. The cattle trembled, and they did not go into the water. Then Of-Good-Fame led the great bull into the water, and the herd followed it. So they crossed the river, and only a small cow sank. The men said: The river has taken its share.

clauses.english: Of-Good-Fame came with his men to a great river.
Its water was deep.
The cattle trembled, and they did not go into the water.
Then Of-Good-Fame led the great bull into the water, and the herd followed it.
So they crossed the river, and only a small cow sank.
The men said:
The river has taken its share.

title: The Two Kings at the Boundary

plan.english: Two kings met at the boundary. The first king said: This river is our boundary. Whoever drives cattle across the river, may he give ten cows. The other king said: Your word is good. Let us two swear an oath to Father Sky. Then they swore, and they set a stone at the river. That stone yonder stands there.

clauses.english: Two kings met at the boundary.
The first king said:
This river is our boundary.
Whoever drives cattle across the river, may he give ten cows.
The other king said:
Your word is good.
Let us two swear an oath to Father Sky.
Then they swore, and they set a stone at the river.
That stone yonder stands there.

plan.english: Ill-Minded stood on the wall and shouted to the pursuing warriors: Your cows are in my stall, and they eat my grass! Come and take them, if you dare! Of-Goodly-Fame answered him: Ill-Minded, your words are wind. In the evening your blood will be red on the earth, and the dogs will lick it. Then he threw his spear, and it struck the mouth of Ill-Minded.

clauses.english: Ill-Minded stood on the wall and shouted to the pursuing warriors:
Your cows are in my stall, and they eat my grass!
Come and take them, if you dare!
Of-Goodly-Fame answered him:
Ill-Minded, your words are wind.
In the evening your blood will be red on the earth, and the dogs will lick it.
Then he threw his spear, and it struck the mouth of Ill-Minded.

plan.english: The men of Ill-Minded seized a young man, the brother of Of-Good-Horses. His sister went alone to the house of the foe. She carried gold and white wool. She said to Ill-Minded: Take this gold and give me my brother. Ill-Minded spoke: The price of your brother is a hundred cows. The sister said: Last year you drove off the cows of my father. Then Ill-Minded was silent, and he let the young man go, and the sister led her brother home. Her name is famous.

clauses.english: The men of Ill-Minded seized a young man, the brother of Of-Good-Horses.
His sister went alone to the house of the foe.
She carried gold and white wool.
She said to Ill-Minded:
Take this gold and give me my brother.
Ill-Minded spoke:
The price of your brother is a hundred cows.
The sister said:
Last year you drove off the cows of my father.
Then Ill-Minded was silent, and he let the young man go, and the sister led her brother home.
Her name is famous.

plan.english: The serpent hid the cows of the gods in a rock. Night lay on the earth, and Dawn did not come. Then a hero, Of-Divine-Race, came with his song. He sang to the rock, and the rock split. He slew the serpent and drove out the cows of the gods. Then Dawn, the daughter of Sky, shone forth. The gods praised the hero: Of-Divine-Race, your fame is imperishable!

clauses.english: The serpent hid the cows of the gods in a rock.
Night lay on the earth, and Dawn did not come.
Then a hero, Of-Divine-Race, came with his song.
He sang to the rock, and the rock split.
He slew the serpent and drove out the cows of the gods.
Then Dawn, the daughter of Sky, shone forth.
The gods praised the hero:
Of-Divine-Race, your fame is imperishable!

title: The Third One and the Serpent

plan.english: A serpent stole the cattle of men. It had three heads. It drove them into the mountain. Then the Third One, a young warrior, seized his spear. He went to the mountain and cried: Serpent, give me the cattle of men! The serpent roared, but the Third One struck its three heads. So he slew the serpent and drove the cattle home. The men gave him the first share of the herd.

clauses.english: A serpent stole the cattle of men.
It had three heads.
It drove them into the mountain.
Then the Third One, a young warrior, seized his spear.
He went to the mountain and cried:
Serpent, give me the cattle of men!
The serpent roared, but the Third One struck its three heads.
So he slew the serpent and drove the cattle home.
The men gave him the first share of the herd.

plan.english: At the ford the men of Kindly overpowered the men of Ill-Minded. Then Ill-Minded, spearless, came to Kindly and spoke: Let us two divide the herd. You take the bulls, and let me take the cows. Kindly said: Why should I divide my own cattle? You will live; go home, and do not come again into my fields. Then Ill-Minded went away, and Kindly drove the herd home.

clauses.english: At the ford the men of Kindly overpowered the men of Ill-Minded.
Then Ill-Minded, spearless, came to Kindly and spoke:
Let us two divide the herd.
You take the bulls, and let me take the cows.
Kindly said:
Why should I divide my own cattle?
You will live; go home, and do not come again into my fields.
Then Ill-Minded went away, and Kindly drove the herd home.

plan.english: Two young men were guarding the herd on a hill. In the night they saw a fire yonder. The first young man asked: Who are those men yonder? The other said: They are thieves; at dawn they will come to our cattle. Run to the house and call the warriors! The young man ran, and the warriors rose up in the night. At dawn the thieves came; they found spears, they did not find cattle. So the two young men rescued the herd.

clauses.english: Two young men were guarding the herd on a hill.
In the night they saw a fire yonder.
The first young man asked:
Who are those men yonder?
The other said:
They are thieves; at dawn they will come to our cattle.
Run to the house and call the warriors!
The young man ran, and the warriors rose up in the night.
At dawn the thieves came; they found spears, they did not find cattle.
So the two young men rescued the herd.

plan.english: Of-Good-Horses yoked the swift horses to the chariot. He stood up in the chariot and seized the harness ropes. The horses ran through the fields, and the wheels roared. At the ford he came to the thieves. Thieves, stand! My horses are swift, and your feet have grown tired. Then the thieves left the cattle and fled to the mountain. Of-Good-Horses did not pursue them; he drew the herd home.

clauses.english: Of-Good-Horses yoked the swift horses to the chariot.

The horses ran through the fields, and the wheels roared.
At the ford he came to the thieves.
Thieves, stand!
My horses are swift, and your feet have grown tired.
Then the thieves left the cattle and fled to the mountain.
Of-Good-Horses did not pursue them; he drew the herd home.

plan.english: The thieves hid the cattle among the trees. The warriors sought them, but they did not find them. In the evening a bull roared among the trees. Then the warriors laughed: The bull is calling us! They went in among the trees and drove out the cattle. The thieves fled. A thief hides cattle, but cattle do not hide themselves.

clauses.english: The thieves hid the cattle among the trees.
The warriors sought them, but they did not find them.
In the evening a bull roared among the trees.
Then the warriors laughed:
The bull is calling us!
They went in among the trees and drove out the cattle.
The thieves fled.
A thief hides cattle, but cattle do not hide themselves.

plan.english: The warriors came home unharmed with the cattle of the foe. The women and the children came out of the houses. The wife of Of-Good-Fame saw her husband and asked: Where is my brother? Of-Good-Fame said: He lies at the ford, but his fame lives. Then they killed a bull and cooked the meat in a cauldron. An old man sang the true fame of the brother.

clauses.english: The warriors came home unharmed with the cattle of the foe.

Where is my brother?
Of-Good-Fame said:
He lies at the ford, but his fame lives.
Then they killed a bull and cooked the meat in a cauldron.
An old man sang the true fame of the brother.

title: The Quarrel over the White Bull

plan.english: Two warriors wanted a white bull. The first said: I was the first in the stall of the foe. The other said: But I led it home with my own hand. Then the clan chief spoke to the two: May the bull choose its own master. He set the bull between the two warriors. The other warrior had given water to the bull. Then the bull went to him, and the first warrior was silent.

clauses.english: Two warriors wanted a white bull.
The first said:
I was the first in the stall of the foe.
The other said:
But I led it home with my own hand.
Then the clan chief spoke to the two:
May the bull choose its own master.
He set the bull between the two warriors.
The other warrior had given water to the bull.
Then the bull went to him, and the first warrior was silent.

plan.english: A stranger came to the house of Of-Goodly-Fame. Of-Goodly-Fame gave him meat and mead. The stranger slept in the house, but in the night he rose up and drove off the white cow. In the morning Of-Goodly-Fame followed him and found him at the river. Guest, why did you deceive me? I gave you meat and mead. The stranger said: I am not your guest; I am your foe. Then the two fought at the river, and Of-Goodly-Fame slew the stranger. The white cow went home.

clauses.english: A stranger came to the house of Of-Goodly-Fame.
Of-Goodly-Fame gave him meat and mead.
The stranger slept in the house, but in the night he rose up and drove off the white cow.

Guest, why did you deceive me?
I gave you meat and mead.
The stranger said:
I am not your guest; I am your foe.
Then the two fought at the river, and Of-Goodly-Fame slew the stranger.
The white cow went home.

plan.english: Of-True-Fame sent out a young man to the foes. The young man stood up in front of the house of the foes and spoke the words of his master: Give us the cattle, or we shall burn your houses. We shall come with fire and spears. The foes said: We are not afraid of your fire. Our walls are strong, and our spears are sharp. Then the young man went and told these words to his master.

clauses.english: Of-True-Fame sent out a young man to the foes.
The young man stood up in front of the house of the foes and spoke the words of his master:

The foes said:
We are not afraid of your fire.
Our walls are strong, and our spears are sharp.
Then the young man went and told these words to his master.

plan.english: The young men wore the skins of wolves. They dwelt on the hills, and they ate raw meat. At the end of the year they drove the cattle of the foes. They brought them in to their fathers. The fathers said: Now you are men; you are not wolves. Your fame will be great.

clauses.english: The young men wore the skins of wolves.
They dwelt on the hills, and they ate raw meat.
At the end of the year they drove the cattle of the foes.
They brought them in to their fathers.
The fathers said:
Now you are men; you are not wolves.
Your fame will be great.

plan.english: Ill-Minded swore a pledge to Of-Good-Fame. But in the night he drove off the cattle of Of-Good-Fame again. Of-Good-Fame cried toward the sky: Father Sky, you have seen the pledge, and you have seen the lie! Then thunder roared over the hills, and Perkwunos struck the stall of Ill-Minded. The stall burned, and the cattle fled out of it. They ran to their own master. Whoever deceives his friend, Perkwunos strikes him.

clauses.english: Ill-Minded swore a pledge to Of-Good-Fame.
But in the night he drove off the cattle of Of-Good-Fame again.
Of-Good-Fame cried toward the sky:
Father Sky, you have seen the pledge, and you have seen the lie!
Then thunder roared over the hills, and Perkwunos struck the stall of Ill-Minded.
The stall burned, and the cattle fled out of it.
They ran to their own master.
Whoever deceives his friend, Perkwunos strikes him.

plan.english: The warriors came home unharmed, and the old king asked them: How many cows did you drive? We drove so many cows as there are stars in the sky. The king laughed: Do not deceive me! How many did you drive? A young man said: We drove a hundred cows, ten bulls and a white horse. The king spoke: Your word is true. Lead the white horse to me!

clauses.english: The warriors came home unharmed, and the old king asked them:

We drove so many cows as there are stars in the sky.
The king laughed:
Do not deceive me!
How many did you drive?
A young man said:
We drove a hundred cows, ten bulls and a white horse.
The king spoke:
Your word is true.
Lead the white horse to me!

title: The Hero Speaks to His Horses

plan.english: Fame-from-the-Gods spoke to his two horses: Swift horses, carry me to the stalls of the foes, and lead me home alive. If I die, may you not leave my body to the dogs. Then the horses bowed their heads and ran toward the foes.

clauses.english: Fame-from-the-Gods spoke to his two horses:
Swift horses, carry me to the stalls of the foes, and lead me home alive.
If I die, may you not leave my body to the dogs.
Then the horses bowed their heads and ran toward the foes.

plan.english: Of-Good-Horses set a cup of mead by the river and called upon the gods: Gods, givers of good things, hear me! Give me the cattle of the foe, and I shall give you the first bull. May my horses be swift, and may my spear not break! Then with his men he crossed over the river. At dawn he came home unharmed with a hundred cows, and he gave the first bull to the gods.

clauses.english: Of-Good-Horses set a cup of mead by the river and called upon the gods:
Gods, givers of good things, hear me!
Give me the cattle of the foe, and I shall give you the first bull.
May my horses be swift, and may my spear not break!
Then with his men he crossed over the river.
At dawn he came home unharmed with a hundred cows, and he gave the first bull to the gods.

plan.english: Two brothers went out with spears. The first brother drove the cattle; the other guarded the path. Foes came on the path, and a spear struck the other brother. He fell and died. The first brother carried his body home and said to their mother: I bring you cattle, but I do not bring your son. The mother was silent, then she said: Cattle I have; a son I do not have.

clauses.english: Two brothers went out with spears.

He fell and died.
The first brother carried his body home and said to their mother:
I bring you cattle, but I do not bring your son.
The mother was silent, then she said:
Cattle I have; a son I do not have.

plan.english: Kindly had seized the daughter of Ill-Minded, and Ill-Minded had seized the son of Kindly. The two fathers met at the ford. Kindly spoke: Give me my son, and I shall give you your daughter. Ill-Minded said: Your son is strong, and my daughter is small; give me ten cows besides. Kindly said: I shall not give you a cow. Then Ill-Minded laughed, and the two fathers exchanged their children.

clauses.english: Kindly had seized the daughter of Ill-Minded, and Ill-Minded had seized the son of Kindly.
The two fathers met at the ford.
Kindly spoke:
Give me my son, and I shall give you your daughter.
Ill-Minded said:
Your son is strong, and my daughter is small; give me ten cows besides.
Kindly said:
I shall not give you a cow.
Then Ill-Minded laughed, and the two fathers exchanged their children.

plan.english: Of-Good-Fame had a white, long-horned bull. The people knew that bull. In the morning Of-Good-Fame did not find the bull in the stall. He followed its tracks to the house of Of-Good-Horses. Of-Good-Horses, my bull is in your stall. Of-Good-Horses said: The gods sent it to me. Of-Good-Fame said: Then the gods will send me your bull. Of-Good-Horses laughed and gave him the long-horned bull.

The people knew that bull.

Of-Good-Horses, my bull is in your stall.
Of-Good-Horses said:
The gods sent it to me.
Of-Good-Fame said:
Then the gods will send me your bull.
Of-Good-Horses laughed and gave him the long-horned bull.

plan.english: On the road a warrior met a herdsman driving many cattle. Who is the master of these cattle? The herdsman said: Their master is the king of this people. Where are you driving them? I am driving them to the river; they are thirsty. The warrior said: Give me ten cows, and you will go. The herdsman answered: The warriors of the king are coming on the road. Then the warrior saw them and went away.

Their master is the king of this people.
Where are you driving them?
I am driving them to the river; they are thirsty.
The warrior said:
Give me ten cows, and you will go.
The herdsman answered:
The warriors of the king are coming on the road.
Then the warrior saw them and went away.

title: The Last Stand at the Stall

plan.english: Ten men of Ill-Minded came to the stall of Kindly. Kindly was alone; his brothers were at the feast. He stood up in front of the door with spear and bow: Men of Ill-Minded, if you want these cattle, take them from my hands! He slew three men, but the others struck him down. Kindly fell in front of the door, and the cattle stood around him. In the evening his brothers came and found him. The fame of Kindly is imperishable.

plan.english: At night the warriors sat around the fire, and their hearts were glad. A young man sang a new song: In the night we crossed the river. We drove the cows of the foe, and the foe slept. Now the cows give us milk, and the milk is sweet. The warriors laughed and drank. But an old man spoke: Be silent! The foe has ears.

plan.english: The two clan chiefs sat down together at a feast. Of-True-Fame gave Man-Minded a cup of mead: Drink, guest! Be dear to us! Man-Minded drank and said: May the gods give you good things. Take these three horses from me. May our two herds eat grass together at the boundary. So the two men became friends.
